profiles.category: Natural and applied sciences and related occupations
profiles.sourceScopeExcerpt: Engineers are regulated everywhere in Canada. In order to use one of the reserved titles, you are required to be registered with a provincial or territorial regulatory authority to be authorized to practise as an engineer anywhere in Canada. If you work under the direct supervision of licensed professional engineers, note that the use of one of the reserved titles is not required in order to practise anywhere in Canada, and therefore, certification is voluntary. Engineer (ing.) and professional engineer (P. Eng.) are the titles used in regulations governing this occupation.

profiles.category: Natural and applied sciences and related occupations
profiles.sourceScopeExcerpt: Agrologists are regulated everywhere in Canada except Northwest Territories, Nunavut, and Yukon. This means that to use the reserved title, you must be registered with one of the provincial regulatory authorities to be authorized to practise as an agrologist anywhere in Canada except Northwest Territories, Nunavut, and Yukon. Professional agrologist (P.Ag), technical agrologist (Tech.Ag), registered technologist in agrology (RTAg), agricultural technologist (AT), and articling agrologist (A.Ag) are some of the titles used in the regulations governing this occupation.

profiles.directoryTitle: Air pilots, flight engineers and flying instructors
profiles.sourceScopeExcerpt: Air pilots, flight engineers, and flying instructors are regulated everywhere in Canada. You are required to be registered with the federal regulatory authority to be authorized to practise as an air pilot, flight engineer, and flying instructor anywhere in Canada. Canadian Commercial Pilot Licence — Aeroplane (CPL-A ), Airline Transport Pilot Licence — Aeroplane (ATPL-A), Multi-crew Pilot Licence (MPL), Flight Engineer (FLENG) licence, Private Pilot Licence (PPL), and Foreign Licence Validation Certificate (FLVC) are cited in regulations governing this occupation.

profiles.directoryTitle: Air traffic controllers and related occupations
profiles.sourceScopeExcerpt: Air traffic controllers and related occupations are regulated everywhere in Canada. You are required to be registered with the federal regulatory authority to be authorized to practise as an air traffic controller anywhere in Canada. Air traffic control licence or ratings [including instrument flight rules (IFR) and visual flight rules (VFR)], certified flight dispatchers (and/or flight followers), and certified flight service specialists are cited in regulations governing this occupation.

profiles.category: Natural and applied sciences and related occupations
profiles.sourceScopeExcerpt: Aircraft instrument, electrical and avionics mechanics, technicians, and inspectors are regulated everywhere in Canada. You are required to be registered with the federal regulatory authority to be authorized to practise as an aircraft instrument, electrical and avionics mechanic, technician, and inspector anywhere in Canada. profiles.directoryTitle: Animal health technologists and veterinary technicians
profiles.sourceScopeExcerpt: Animal health technologists and veterinary technicians are regulated in Alberta, British Columbia, Manitoba, Ontario, and Saskatchewan. This means that you must be registered with one of the provincial regulatory authorities to be authorized to practise as an animal health technologist and/or veterinary technician in Alberta and Manitoba. In British Columbia, Ontario and Saskatchewan, registration is required by law only if you wish to use the reserved titles. Registered animal health technologist (RAHT), registered veterinary technician, and registered veterinary technologist (RVT) are the titles used in the regulations governing these occupations.

If a trade is regulated in the province or territory you wish to settle in, contact the regulatory authority and/or apprenticeship office in that province or territory. When a trade is regulated, it means that you are required to be registered with a provincial or territorial regulatory authority to be authorized to practise that trade in that province or territory.

profiles.sourceScopeExcerpt: Applied science or engineering technicians and technologists are regulated everywhere in Canada except Yukon, Northwest Territories and Nunavut. This means that to use one of the reserved titles, you are required to be registered with a provincial regulatory authority to be authorized to practise as a technician or technologist anywhere in Canada, except in Yukon, Northwest Territories and Nunavut. The following titles are used in the regulations governing these occupations: Applied science technologist (A.Sc.T./AScT); Certified computer information technologist (CCIT); Certified engineering technologist (C.E.T./CET); Certified technician (CTech); Professional technologist (PTech); Professional technician (P.T.); Registered engineering technologist (RET); Technologue professionnel (TP).

Property assessors who use the protected title are regulated in Alberta, Quebec, and Saskatchewan only. This means that you must be registered with one of the provincial regulatory authorities to be authorized to use the title in Alberta, Quebec, and Saskatchewan. Chartered appraiser, chartered assessor, accredited municipal assessor of Alberta (AMAA), municipal assessment appraiser of Saskatchewan (MAAS), and municipal rural assessment appraiser of Saskatchewan (MRAAS) are titles used in regulations governing this occupational category.

Audiologists and speech-language pathologists are regulated* in Alberta, British Columbia, Manitoba, New Brunswick, Newfoundland and Labrador, Ontario, Quebec, and Saskatchewan. This means that you must be registered with one of the provincial regulatory authorities to be authorized to practise as an audiologist and/or speech-language pathologist in those provinces. Speech therapist, speech-language pathologist, and audiologist are the titles used in the regulations governing these occupations. *The academic/clinical training and scope of practice for these occupations are distinctly different in Canada and may be separately regulated, depending on the province or territory you wish to work in.

profiles.directoryTitle: Cardiology technologists and electrophysiological diagnostic technologists
profiles.sourceScopeExcerpt: Electroencephalograph (EEG) technologists are regulated only in Alberta and Quebec. This means that to be authorized to practise as an EEG technologist anywhere in Alberta or Quebec, you must: register with and obtain certification from one of the registration boards; be a member of the national professional association. These requirements are set by the respective provincial and territorial Colleges of Physicians and Surgeons. Electroneurophysiology (ENP) technologists are regulated in Alberta and Quebec. This means that to be authorized to practise as an ENP technologist in Alberta or Quebec, you must register with and obtain certification from one of the regulatory authorities in those provinces. Note that electromyography (EMG) and cardiology technologists are identified/regulated as distinct occupations in some provinces and territories. For more information, consult the occupational profiles for: Electromyography (EMG) Technologist (Cardiology technologists and electrophysiological diagnostic technologists, n.e.c.) ; and/or Cardiology Technologists (Cardiology technologists and electrophysiological diagnostic technologists, n.e.c.)

profiles.directoryTitle: Dental assistants and dental laboratory assistants
profiles.sourceScopeExcerpt: Dental assistants are regulated everywhere in Canada except Ontario, Northwest Territories, Nunavut, Quebec, and Yukon. This means that you must be registered with one of the provincial regulatory authorities in order to use the reserved title and be authorized to practise as a dental assistant anywhere in Canada except in Ontario, Northwest Territories, Nunavut, Quebec, and Yukon. Dental assistant (DA) and registered dental assistants (RDA) are the titles used in regulations governing these occupations.

Dental hygienists are regulated everywhere in Canada. In order to use one of the reserved titles, you are required to be registered with a provincial or territorial regulatory authority to be authorized to practise as a dental hygienist anywhere in Canada. Dental hygienist (DH), registered dental hygienist (RDH), and restorative dental hygienist are some of the titles used in regulations governing this occupation. Note that dental therapists are identified/regulated as distinct occupations in some provinces and territories. For more information, consult the occupational profile for: dental therapists .

Dental technologists, technicians, and laboratory assistants are regulated everywhere in Canada except Manitoba, Northwest Territories, Nunavut, Prince Edward Island, and Yukon. This means that you must be registered with one of the provincial regulatory authorities in order to use the reserved title and be authorized to practise as a dental technologist, technician, and laboratory assistant anywhere except Manitoba, Northwest Territories, Nunavut, Prince Edward Island, and Yukon. Note that the use of one of the reserved titles is not required in order to practise in Nova Scotia, and therefore, certification there is voluntary. Dental technologist (DT), registered dental technologist (RDT), dental technician (DT), registered dental technician (RDT), and certified dental technician (CDT) are some of the titles used in regulations governing these occupations.

Dentists and oral surgeons are regulated everywhere in Canada. This means that you must be registered with one of the provincial or territorial regulatory authorities to be authorized to practise as a dentist and/or oral surgeon anywhere in Canada. Dentist, oral surgeon, orthodontist, or periodontist are titles used in regulations governing these occupations.

Denturists are regulated everywhere in Canada. In order to use one of the reserved titles, you are required to be registered with a provincial or territorial regulatory authority to be authorized to practise as a denturist anywhere in Canada. Denturist, registered denturist, denturologist, dental mechanic, and denture therapist are the titles used in regulations governing this occupation.

Dietitians are regulated everywhere in Canada except Northwest Territories, Nunavut, and Yukon. This means that to use the reserved title, you must be registered with one of the provincial regulatory authorities to be authorized to practise as a dietitian anywhere in Canada, except in Northwest Territories, Nunavut, and Yukon. Registered dietitian (RD), professional dietitian (PDt), or dietician/dietitian are the titles used in the regulations governing this occupation. Note that nutritionists are identified/regulated as a distinct occupation in some provinces. For more information, consult the occupational profile for: Nutritionists (Dietitians and nutritionists) .

profiles.sourceScopeExcerpt: Educational counsellors are regulated everywhere in Canada. This means that you must be registered with one of the provincial or territorial regulatory authorities to be authorized to practise as an educational counsellor anywhere in Canada. This is usually done through certification as: a teacher , within the elementary and secondary school systems; a psychologist and/or social worker , within the postsecondary education systems; an educational counsellor , within all education systems (in Quebec only). For more information, consult the occupational profiles for: elementary school and kindergarten teachers ; secondary school teachers ; psychologists ; and/or social workers .
